title: Formula E finds a new home on Disney+, ESPN+
gist: Formula E has signed a multiyear deal to broadcast every session of each ePrix on Disney+ and ESPN+ across 144 countries starting with season 12 in December, moving off Roku in the US just as the GEN4 car doubles power output and pushes the series onto traditional road courses.

insights.claim: Formula E's new multiyear deal puts live coverage of every ePrix — practice, qualifying and race — on Disney+ and ESPN+ in 144 countries beginning with season 12 in December.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Full-session rights on a major global streamer is the standard playbook for converting a niche motorsport into a mainstream media property; watch subscriber-driven sponsorship pricing next.
insights.quote: It has signed a new multiyear deal to broadcast the sport on Disney+ and ESPN+ in 144 countries, with live coverage of each entire ePrix, from practice through qualifying to the race.
insights.locator: Formula E is set to make a big change

insights.claim: In the US the series is leaving Roku, which has carried it live since 2023, for Disney's streaming platforms — a move up the distribution ladder from a device-maker's free channel to a subscription sports service.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Roku losing a live sports property signals the limits of its content strategy against incumbents willing to pay for rights; sports rights continue migrating to bundled streamers.
insights.quote: since 2023, the sport has been shown live on Roku
insights.locator: The new media deal means that here in the US

insights.claim: Formula E's CEO Jeff Dodds explicitly ties the deal to global growth ambitions and the GEN4 era rather than to near-term revenue, framing Disney's reach and storytelling as fan-acquisition infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Management is prioritizing audience scale over rights fees, which usually means the deal economics favor the distributor near term and the series later.
insights.quote: Disney’s unrivaled global reach and storytelling will introduce Formula E to millions of new fans while bringing them closer than ever to the drama, innovation, and excitement of electric racing.
insights.locator: This is a landmark moment for Formula E

insights.claim: The GEN4 car debuting in December doubles the current car's power, producing a nominal 603 hp (450 kW) from a twin-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain and up to 804 hp (600 kW) in Attack Mode.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A doubling of output in one generation is the kind of visible spec jump that changes the marketing story for EV racing and for the OEM suppliers behind the powertrains.
insights.quote: The new car has double the power of the current racer, with a nominal 603 hp (450 kW) from a twin-motor, all-wheel drive powertrain that goes up to 804 hp (600 kW) in Attack Mode.
insights.locator: As we’ve previously covered here at Ars

insights.claim: For much of a lap a GEN4 Formula E car will match a 2027-spec Formula 1 car on power, because the F1 car falls to 602 hp from its V6 alone once the hybrid battery is depleted.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Power parity with F1 removes the most-cited technical dismissal of Formula E and strengthens its pitch to OEMs and sponsors weighing motorsport budgets.
insights.quote: the F1 car is also stuck with just 602 hp from its V6 engine when the battery has no charge
insights.locator: Which means that for much of a lap

insights.claim: F1 cars will still be quicker over a lap because of lower mass, more aerodynamic downforce and slick tires, while the Formula E car remains 18 percent heavier and runs treaded tires with less downforce.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The remaining gap is mass and aero, not propulsion — a precise map of where battery-electric racing still trails and where the engineering investment must go.
insights.quote: F1 cars will still be faster over a lap of a given circuit thanks to less mass, more aerodynamic downforce, and the use of slick tires.
insights.locator: F1 cars will still be faster over a lap

insights.claim: Formula E gains better low-speed acceleration than F1 from its pair of electric motors, the one performance dimension where the electric formula is structurally advantaged.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Instant-torque advantage is the durable selling point for electric racing formats and for the road-car marketing that funds them.
insights.quote: Formula E’s car should have better acceleration from low speed thanks to a pair of electric motors
insights.locator: F1 cars will still be faster over a lap

insights.claim: Higher GEN4 speeds are forcing Formula E to abandon some of the tight city-center street circuits that defined its identity in favor of traditional road courses including Brands Hatch and the Circuit of the Americas.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The urban-racing differentiator is being traded for spectacle and speed, moving Formula E toward direct comparison with conventional series — a repositioning risk and an opportunity in one.
insights.quote: dropping some of the tight city center street circuits it originally raced at in favor of some traditional road courses like Brands Hatch in the UK and the Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas
insights.locator: Still, the much faster nature of the GEN4 machines
